People's Majlis Committee Minutes

18th Meeting of the General Committee

21 October 2026

Venue: People's Majlis building (Committee Room 12)

Start time: 11:34

{Chaired by the Committee Chair; Member for Hulhudhoo constituency Mohamed Shahid}

Remarks from the Chair:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I welcome all honourable members to the 18th meeting of the General Committee. I will read out the names for attendance, to complete the minutes. Accordingly, participating in today's committee are Abdul Sattar Mohamed, Holhudhoo constituency. Ahmed Riyaz, Thimarafushi constituency. Abdul Latheef Abdul Rahman, Alifushi constituency constituency. Ibrahim Didi, Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency. Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru, Thulhaadhoo constituency. Hussain Riza Adam, Maafushi constituency. Mohamed Ali, Dhuvaafaru constituency. Ameen Faisal, Kanditheemu constituency, and myself, Mohamed Shahid, Hulhudhoo constituency. There are two items on our agenda today. The first, item number one on the agenda, is to study the matter sent seeking advice on signing the agreement concerning the Inter-Parliamentary Speakers' Conference. Second is to study the matter sent seeking advice on signing a Memorandum of Understanding on Parliamentary Cooperation with "The House of Councillors of the Kingdom of Morocco". Now, for us in the committee, the Dhivehi translations of these agreements should now be in all honourable members' files too. Yes! The purpose for which this agreement is signed, in other words, all the detailed documents of this will now be in all honourable members' files. So, what I ask is that, when we give such advice from the committee, all honourable members consider it as deeply as possible, and that after study, with time given, we proceed with this committee so that the committee reaches a decision. In that regard, there is also a Dhivehi translation here of the matter sent seeking advice on signing the agreement concerning the Inter-Parliamentary Speakers' Conference. I will read this briefly, just for the record. Yes! Yes! Now, we will still get a copy, won't we, for us in the committee, the committee. (After a short pause) So, I will just say, for the information of the honourable members of this committee, the purpose of the Inter-Parliamentary Speakers' Conference too. This purpose, the main purpose of this agreement, is to build on international relations in which all parties participate without national, religious or racial discrimination, and to promote peace, stability and, in addition to

[stamp]

adapting to climate change and restoring the environment, sustainable development. And to work to achieve the following specific goals. 1- To work to resolve conflicts peacefully in accordance with international laws and principles, and to establish lasting peace and development. 2- To prevent conflicts, giving priority to tolerance. 3- To find peaceful solutions to conflicts through consultation and by playing the role of a mediator. 4- To support rebuilding society and sustaining peace after conflicts. 5- To work to ensure water, energy and food security at the regional level. 6- To work to respond to climate disasters and achieve the UN's 2030 Sustainable Development Goals, the SDGs. To contribute to sustaining peace by increasing the participation of civil society organisations and educational institutions. 8- To promote the respect and unity that must be maintained between religions and cultures. This is the main purpose of this. So, I will open the floor to the committee members. I give the floor to the honourable Ibrahim Didi of Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency.

Remarks by the Member for Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency, Ibrahim Didi:

Yes! Thank you, honourable Chair. As the Chair just said, this agreement contains important, good things to do. Among them are strengthening cooperation between the speakers of countries, carrying out various work through consultation on various matters of peace, and important matters relating to the environment are also included in this. Working to strengthen matters of the basic services the people receive is also included in this. So, I consider this a very good agreement. However, some honourable members among us are requesting some time to study it further. So, I propose that we study these two agreements, this agreement and the one with Morocco that we have decided to enter into, and decide this matter at the meeting to be held next week. So, by holding a meeting next Monday, or on some day next week, this

[stamp]

I propose that a time be set for the meeting and that time be given as the honourable members wish.

Remarks from the Chair:

I give the floor to Abdul Sattar Mohamed, Holhudhoo constituency.

Remarks by the Member for Holhudhoo constituency, Abdul Sattar Mohamed:

Yes! I would like to say that I second the proposal made by the honourable Ibrahim Didi of Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency.

Remarks from the Chair

Yes! There is no proposal from any other honourable member. As I said earlier, the honourable Member for Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency also made this proposal in order to study it. And it was seconded by Abdul Sattar Mohamed, Holhudhoo constituency. So, we, (after a short pause) so, with no further views from any other member, I ask the honourable members who agree to vote in the way proposed by the honourable Member for Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency and seconded by the honourable Member for Holhudhoo constituency, Abdul Sattar Mohamed. (Voting) Yes! Thank you. What was passed by consensus of the committee is to give us more time to study this. Therefore, we will proceed on this so as to reach a decision at the next committee meeting. With no further work for today's committee from this point, we will conclude the committee. Thank you very much.

[stamp]
